subject: Islamic Studies
board: TGA Islamic Studies scheme (aqeedah, fiqh, seerah, hadith, akhlaq)
source: Adapted from TGA Drive RE/Islamic Studies folder (Al-Baseerah Salah quiz EYFS/KS1: thanking Allah, blessings, praying on time, best deeds); Early Years themes

lessons.title: Allah made everything
objectives: Know that Allah made everything
Say SubhanAllah when we see Allah's creation
Know that Allah is One

keywords.def: the One God who made everything

starter: Say 'Bismillah' with me. When do we say it?
Show me your listening ears and your looking eyes.
Can you name one thing you can see in your home?

teach.heading: Allah made the world
bullets: Allah made the sun, moon and stars
Allah made trees, rivers and animals
teach.note: Bismillah first. Use a slow picture slideshow: sun, sea, flower, baby. After each picture ask: who made this? Children answer 'Allah'. Keep sentences short and warm.

teach.heading: Allah is One
bullets: Nobody helps Allah to make things
teach.note: Hold up one finger. Say: Allah is One. Children echo. Misconception: young children may ask 'who made Allah?'. Answer simply: Allah was never made, Allah is always there. Do not go further.

teach.heading: SubhanAllah
bullets: We say 'SubhanAllah' when we see something amazing
It means: Glory be to Allah
Say it for a rainbow, a bird, a flower
teach.note: Teach the phrase with echo and a hand gesture (hands opening like a flower). Play 'amazing picture' game: show a picture, children whisper SubhanAllah.

teach.heading: Allah made me
bullets: Allah gave me eyes to see
Allah gave me ears to hear
Allah gave me hands to help
teach.note: Children point to each body part as you name it. Ask: what can your hands do that is kind? Link to thanking Allah, which is the next lesson.

practice: Point to a picture of an animal. Who made it?
independent: Draw one thing Allah made and say 'SubhanAllah' to your partner
Match pictures of the sun, a tree and a fish to the word 'Allah made'
Fill the sentence: Allah made ______ (children choose a picture)
exit: Who made the sun and the trees?
What do we say when something is amazing?
lessons.homework: Spot one amazing thing Allah made at home and say SubhanAllah when you see it.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: picture cards and gesture for each phrase; repeat SubhanAllah with actions. Stretch: say why we say SubhanAllah in a full sentence.

lessons.title: Alhamdulillah: thanking Allah
objectives: Know that Allah gives us many blessings
Say Alhamdulillah to thank Allah
Say thank you to people who are kind to us

keywords.def: All praise and thanks belong to Allah
kind words when someone helps us

starter: Who made the sun and the moon? What do we say when we see something amazing?
Say 'Bismillah' slowly.
Name one animal Allah made.

teach.heading: Allah gives us blessings
bullets: Food, water and a warm home
teach.note: Show pictures of blessings. Ask what children are happy to have. Explain: a blessing is a gift from Allah. Allah says in the Qur'an that we could never count all His blessings (16:18). Say this simply: there are too many to count.

teach.heading: Alhamdulillah
bullets: Say it after eating and drinking
Say it when we feel happy
teach.note: Echo the word three times, softly then loudly. Role-play: pretend to drink water, then say Alhamdulillah. Explain it means thank you to Allah.

teach.heading: Thank people too
bullets: Say 'thank you' to Mummy and Daddy
teach.note: Teach thank you first, then the Muslim phrase. The Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah (Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi). Say it as: we thank Allah and the people who are kind.

teach.heading: Our thank-you song
teach.note: Chant the three lines with actions (eat, house roof, hug). Children add their own line. Praise each child's idea.

practice: Act out: someone gives you a toy. What do you say?
independent: Draw three blessings from Allah and say Alhamdulillah for each
Sort cards: say Alhamdulillah / say thank you / say both
Circle the happy faces who said thank you
exit: What do we say to thank Allah?
What do we say when a friend helps us?
lessons.homework: Say Alhamdulillah after your dinner and thank someone at home.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use picture prompts and a word mat with the Arabic phrases in English letters. Stretch: say two blessings in a sentence.

lessons.title: Bismillah and eating manners
objectives: Say Bismillah before eating
Eat with the right hand
Say Alhamdulillah after eating

keywords.def: the hand we use to eat and drink
the kind and polite way to do things

starter: Echo: 'Bismillah' and 'Alhamdulillah'.
What do we say to thank Allah?
Show me your right hand.

teach.heading: Before we eat
teach.note: Use a pretend picnic. Model washing hands, sitting down, saying Bismillah. Ask why we say Bismillah: we are remembering Allah who gave us food.

teach.heading: Eat with the right hand
bullets: Use your right hand for eating
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ told the boy Umar ibn Abi Salamah: say Bismillah, eat with your right hand and eat from what is near you (Bukhari and Muslim). Have children hold up right hands. Left-handed children: be gentle, they can practise and the teacher should be kind about it.

teach.heading: After we eat
teach.note: Echo Alhamdulillah. Ask who cooks for them. Link to last lesson: thank Allah and thank people. Do not waste food: Allah gave it to us as a blessing.

teach.heading: Picnic game
teach.note: Children act the full sequence with pretend food. Praise good manners by name. Repeat the sequence in a chant: wash, sit, Bismillah, eat.

practice: What do we do first before we eat? Wash our hands.
Act out the picnic: wash, sit, Bismillah, eat, Alhamdulillah.
independent: Put the pictures in order: wash hands, say Bismillah, eat, say Alhamdulillah
Colour the child who is eating with good manners
Draw your favourite food and say Bismillah before you 'eat' it
exit: What do we say before eating?
Which hand do we use to eat?
lessons.homework: Say Bismillah and eat with your right hand at every meal this week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sequencing pictures with gesture. Stretch: explain why we say Bismillah.

lessons.title: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Allah's messenger
objectives: Know that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is Allah's messenger
Know he was born in Makkah
Say 'sallallahu alayhi wa sallam' after his name

keywords.def: a person Allah chooses to teach us
the city where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born

starter: What do we say before we eat?
Who made everything?
Show me your best manners.

teach.heading: A special person
bullets: Allah chose him to teach people
teach.note: Say his name with respect and teach 'sallallahu alayhi wa sallam' as a phrase children repeat each time. Ask who chooses prophets: Allah.

teach.heading: Born in Makkah
bullets: He was born in the city of Makkah
teach.note: Show a clear picture of the Kaaba. Do not show any picture of the Prophet ﷺ: we never draw him. Explain the Kaaba is Allah's House and Muslims face it for prayer.

teach.heading: Allah's message
bullets: Allah sent angel Jibril to him
The Prophet ﷺ taught people to worship Allah
teach.note: Keep it simple: Jibril brought Allah's words. Link to Qur'an lessons if children have met Jibril there. Ask: what is the Qur'an?

teach.heading: We love the Prophet ﷺ
bullets: We say salam and blessings on him
We try to copy his good manners
teach.note: Teach 'sallallahu alayhi wa sallam' with a hand-on-heart action. Explain love means following his kind manners, not just words.

independent: Draw the Kaaba in Makkah (use the picture on screen to copy)
Fill in: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in ______ (Makkah)
Choose the kind actions we copy from the Prophet ﷺ
exit: Where was the Prophet ﷺ born?
Who is the Prophet ﷺ?
lessons.homework: Tell your family one thing you learned about the Prophet ﷺ today.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: picture of Kaaba and gesture for each phrase. Stretch: say the full blessing and what it means.

lessons.title: The Prophet ﷺ was truthful
objectives: Know the Prophet ﷺ always told the truth
Say why telling the truth is good
Tell the truth even when it is hard
starter: Where was the Prophet ﷺ born?
Echo the blessing on the Prophet ﷺ.
Show me kind hands.

teach.heading: Everyone trusted him
teach.note: Explain that even before he was a prophet, the people of Makkah gave him the name Al-Amin because he was honest. Ask: would you trust someone who lies?

teach.heading: The truth is good
bullets: Telling the truth makes people happy
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said truthfulness leads to goodness and goodness leads to Paradise (Bukhari and Muslim). Say it simply: telling the truth takes us towards Jannah. Keep Jannah positive and gentle.

teach.heading: A hard choice
bullets: You break a cup by accident
Do you hide it or say sorry?
Be brave and tell the truth
teach.note: Use a puppet story. Ask children what the puppet should do. Reassure: Allah and Mummy are happy when we are honest, even if we make mistakes.

teach.heading: Truth song
teach.note: Chant with actions. Children show thumbs up for truth and thumbs down for lies in short examples.

practice: Which is the truth: 'I did it, sorry' or 'It was not me' (when it was)?
What name did people give the Prophet ﷺ?
independent: Sort pictures: telling the truth / not telling the truth
Draw a time you told the truth
Act the cup story with a partner: say 'I am sorry, I broke it'
exit: What does truthful mean?
Why do we tell the truth?
lessons.homework: Tell the truth at home this week, even when it feels hard.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: puppets and sentence stems: 'I am sorry. I did it.' Stretch: explain why trust matters.

lessons.title: Salam and smiles
objectives: Say 'Assalamu alaykum' and reply 'Wa alaykumus salam'
Know smiling is a kind act
Greet friends and teachers kindly
starter: What is the Prophet ﷺ's name Al-Amin?
Why do we tell the truth?
Say Alhamdulillah.

teach.heading: The Muslim greeting
bullets: It means: peace be upon you
teach.note: Echo both parts. Practise in pairs. The Prophet ﷺ taught us to spread salam; he said to spread salam among yourselves (Muslim). Explain that it is a dua for peace.

teach.heading: Smile
bullets: A smile is a kind gift
The Prophet ﷺ said smiling is charity
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said smiling in the face of your brother is charity (at-Tirmidhi). Say it as: a smile is a gift. Everyone smiles at a partner.

teach.heading: Kind words
bullets: Say sorry when you are wrong
teach.note: Role-play short scenes: borrowing a pencil, bumping into someone. Praise good words. Link to thank you and sorry from earlier lessons.

teach.heading: Greeting game
bullets: Walk around and greet three friends
teach.note: On screen: children greet in turn by name. Remind about turn-taking and gentle voices. Praise eye contact and smiles.

independent: Draw two friends greeting with a smile and write or trace 'salam'
Match: greeting / reply
Tick the kind words: please, thank you, give me!
exit: What do we say when we meet a Muslim?
What is a smile?
lessons.homework: Greet everyone at home with salam and a smile.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: visual cue cards and choral response. Stretch: say what salam means.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Clean and ready to pray
lessons.title: Allah loves cleanliness
objectives: Know that being clean is part of our deen
Wash hands properly
Know the Prophet ﷺ taught us to be clean

keywords.def: the way of life Allah teaches us
what we use to wash germs away

starter: Echo: 'Assalamu alaykum'.
Who made our hands?
What do we say before eating?

teach.heading: Cleanliness
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said cleanliness is half of faith
teach.note: The hadith is in Sahih Muslim: purity is half of faith. Explain simply: being clean is very important to Allah. Ask when we wash our hands.

teach.heading: How to wash hands
teach.note: Mime handwashing with a 20-second chant. Show on screen with real or pretend soap. Misconception: just wetting hands is enough; show why soap matters.

teach.heading: Keeping clean
teach.note: Show pictures. Children tick what they did this morning. Keep it light and non-judgemental; some children may not have all routines. Praise effort.

teach.heading: Clean and tidy
teach.note: Link to caring for what Allah gave us. Ask: how can we keep our room clean? Praise ideas.

practice: Which hand do we eat with?
Show me how to wash hands.
independent: Put handwashing pictures in order
Colour the child who is clean and tidy
Draw soap bubbles and say 'Alhamdulillah for water'
exit: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about cleanliness?
When do we wash our hands?
lessons.homework: Wash your hands with soap before every meal and say Bismillah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sequence cards and mime. Stretch: explain why we wash with soap.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Clean and ready to pray
lessons.title: Wudu: washing for prayer
objectives: Know that we make wudu before salah
Name the first steps of wudu
Say Bismillah at the start

keywords.def: washing parts of the body to get ready to pray

starter: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about cleanliness?
Why do we say Bismillah?
Wash hands, mime it.

teach.heading: Why wudu?
bullets: Muslims pray to Allah five times a day
Wudu makes us clean for salah
teach.note: Explain that we meet Allah in salah, so we get clean and ready. Do not teach rulings yet; this is first awareness. Ask: how do we get ready to meet a special guest?

teach.heading: Start with Bismillah
teach.note: Model with a bowl of water or actions. We wash three times. For young children, show with a doll or mime. Parents will help at home.

teach.heading: Wash the face
bullets: Wash the arms to the elbow
teach.note: Mime each action. Teach order. Tell children they will learn all steps over time. Praise correct order.

teach.heading: Wudu song
teach.note: Chant with actions. Allah says He loves those who purify themselves (2:222). Say it as: Allah loves those who keep clean. Do the song twice.

practice: Show me washing hands three times.
independent: Put the wudu pictures in order (first five steps)
Draw yourself making wudu
Act the wudu song with a partner
exit: What do we make before salah?
What do we say first?
lessons.homework: Make wudu with an adult and say Bismillah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: step cards with pictures and mime. Stretch: say all the steps in order.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Clean and ready to pray
lessons.title: The masjid and salah
objectives: Know that the masjid is Allah's house
Show good masjid manners
Know salah has standing, bowing and sujood

keywords.def: putting the forehead on the floor to Allah

starter: Show me the first steps of wudu.
What do we say at the start?
Why do we wash before salah?

teach.heading: The masjid
bullets: The masjid is the house of Allah
We go to pray and learn
We are quiet and kind there
teach.note: Show pictures of masajid. Explain it is the place we gather. Ask: how do we behave in a special place? Quiet voices, walking feet.

teach.heading: The adhan
bullets: The adhan calls us to pray
'Allahu Akbar' means Allah is the Greatest
teach.note: Play a short clear adhan recording. Children whisper Allahu Akbar. Explain that Bilal ibn Rabah called the first adhan in Madinah; keep it brief.

teach.heading: Salah actions
bullets: We stand and say Allahu Akbar
We put our forehead on the ground
teach.note: Demonstrate standing, bowing, sujood. Children copy. Remind: this is a taster. Say that in sujood we are closest to Allah (Muslim). Use gentle wording.

teach.heading: Masjid manners
teach.note: Role-play entering the masjid. Sort pictures into good manners. Praise by name.

practice: What do we do before salah?
independent: Colour a masjid and add the word 'Allah'
Match the salah picture to the action: stand / bow / sujood
Sort good and not-good masjid manners pictures
exit: What is the masjid?
Show me one salah action.
lessons.homework: Show your family how we behave in the masjid.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: pictures and mime; use a mat for movement. Stretch: say the three actions in order.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Kind hearts and good manners
lessons.title: Being kind to Mummy and Daddy
objectives: Know Allah tells us to be good to our parents
Say kind things to parents
Name ways to help at home

keywords.def: do what is right when asked

starter: Show me a masjid manner.
Say salam to your partner.
What do we say after eating?

teach.heading: Allah's command
bullets: Allah tells us to be good to our parents
teach.note: Allah commands good treatment of parents in the Qur'an (17:23). Explain: our parents love and care for us, so we are kind to them.

teach.heading: Kind words
teach.note: Role-play asking for something politely. Praise gentle voices. Remember sensitivity: some children may have different family structures; speak of 'the people who look after you'.

teach.heading: Helping hands
teach.note: Ask what children can do to help. Link to the Prophet ﷺ who helped at home. Keep it positive.

teach.heading: Make dua for them
bullets: It asks Allah to be kind to them
teach.note: The dua is from the Qur'an (17:24): rabbi irhamhuma kama rabbayani saghira. Teach only the first part: Rabbir-hamhuma as a gentle echo. Explain: O Lord, have mercy on them.

practice: Name one way to help at home.
Say 'thank you' like you mean it.
independent: Draw yourself helping at home
Tick the kind things to say to parents
Make a 'thank you' card for someone who looks after you
exit: Who does Allah tell us to be good to?
Name one thing you can do to help.
lessons.homework: Do one kind thing for the people at home and say thank you.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: visual choices and sentence stems 'Thank you for ___'. Stretch: say the dua part with meaning.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Kind hearts and good manners
lessons.title: Sharing and being a good friend
objectives: Know sharing makes people happy
Share and take turns
Be kind to friends

keywords.def: let others use or have some of what you have
someone who is kind to us

starter: Who does Allah tell us to be kind to?
Say 'thank you' to a friend.
Show me kind hands.

teach.heading: Share
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught that a believer wants for his brother what he wants for himself (Bukhari and Muslim). Say it as: we want for our friends what we want for ourselves. Role-play sharing.

teach.heading: Take turns
teach.note: Play a simple turn-taking game. Praise 'you go first'. Reassure children who find waiting hard.

teach.heading: Kind to friends
bullets: Say sorry when you hurt someone
teach.note: Use scenarios with puppets: a friend falls over; a friend snatches a toy. What do we do? Teach: say sorry, forgive.

teach.heading: Friendship rules
teach.note: Make a class chart of three rules using children's ideas. Link to the Prophet ﷺ's good manners.

practice: What do we say to greet friends?
independent: Draw yourself sharing with a friend
Sort pictures: sharing / not sharing
Role-play with a partner: say 'you can go first'
exit: Why do we share?
What do we say if we hurt someone?
lessons.homework: Share something with a family member or friend and tell us who.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: puppets and gestures; sentence stems. Stretch: explain what a good friend does.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Kind hearts and good manners
lessons.title: Review: what we have learned about Islam
objectives: Recall what Allah has made
Recall the Prophet's good manners
Show wudu steps and salah actions

keywords.def: the One God who made everything
the one Allah chooses to teach people

starter: What do we say to thank Allah?
Where was the Prophet ﷺ born?
What do we say before we eat?

teach.heading: Allah and thanks
teach.note: Use picture prompts. Children answer by chorus. Pick up any confusion from Lessons 1-3.

teach.heading: The Prophet ﷺ
teach.note: Revisit truthfulness and smiling. Ask children to act a smile and a greeting.

teach.heading: Clean and ready
teach.note: Quick wudu actions together. Check order. Praise correct steps.

teach.heading: Kind hearts
teach.note: Children choose their favourite good manner and show it. Finish with a short dua: Bismillah and Alhamdulillah.

practice: Echo three phrases: Bismillah, Alhamdulillah, SubhanAllah.
independent: Draw your favourite thing from this half-term
Sequence three wudu pictures
Tell a partner one good manner
exit: Name one thing Allah made.
Name one good manner we learned.
lessons.homework: Teach your family the three phrases: Bismillah, Alhamdulillah, SubhanAllah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use picture mats and word-sentence supports. Stretch: explain one new thing to a younger child.
